11.0.s.en: 1. The attempt to recover the ten tribes

11.0.0.en: 1 And when Rehoboam was come to Jerusalem, he gathered of the house of Judah and Benjamin an hundred and fourscore thousand chosen men, which were warriors, to fight against Israel, that he might bring the kingdom again to Rehoboam. 2 But the word of the LORD came to Shemaiah the man of God, saying, 3 “Speak unto Rehoboam the son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all Israel in Judah and Benjamin, saying, 4 Thus saith the LORD, Ye shall not go up, nor fight against your brethren: return every man to his house: for this thing is done of me.” And they obeyed the words of the LORD, and returned from going against Jeroboam.

11.0.1.en: And when Rehoboam was come to Jerusalem, he gathered of the house of Judah and Benjamin an hundred and fourscore thousand chosen men, which were warriors, to fight against Israel, that he might bring the kingdom again to Rehoboam. [1]

11.0.2.en: Most likely Rehoboam gathered the warriors on the counsel of the young men who urged him to answer the people with violence, and so he lost the ten tribes by his violent words.

11.0.3.en: Rehoboam found justifications that moved him to desire to fight Jeroboam and the ten tribes, namely: 1. He looked on these tribes as schismatic and rebellious, needing to be disciplined. 2. As a lawful king from the house of David, he needed to affirm his authority and his military power to gather the twelve tribes together. 3. He was fulfilling the desire of his father Solomon the wise, who sought to kill Jeroboam because he lifted up his hand against him (1 Kgs 11:26, 40). Jeroboam fled to Egypt, and was there until the death of Solomon. Was not Solomon the wisest man on earth at that time? 4. The ten tribes killed Hadoram, whom he had sent to them for reconciliation, and in his view they had killed an innocent man of peace who had done no wrong (2 Chr 10:18). If David declared war on the Ammonites because they insulted his messengers (2 Sam 10:7), then Jeroboam killed the messenger of Rehoboam without cause. So in his view Jeroboam and the ten tribes needed to be disciplined.

11.1.0.en: But the word of the LORD came to Shemaiah the man of God. [2]

11.1.1.en: Rehoboam's repeated error was not returning to the Lord and consulting Him before acting. Therefore the Lord left him to accomplish what was in his mind, so he gathered a hundred and eighty thousand chosen men to fight the ten tribes; then He sent to him Shemaiah the man of God to reveal to him that he had wasted his time and effort in gathering this army, and that he must release them to return to their houses.

11.1.2.en: It was fitting for Rehoboam to consult the Lord in everything like his grandfather David, most of whose psalms affirm his trust in the counsel of the Lord and His power and care for him (2 Sam 2:1). He used to ask the Lord in every small and great matter, confident that He leads him to victory and grants him success in everything.

11.1.3.en: v “Deliver me, O LORD, from mine enemies: I flee unto thee.”

11.1.4.en: I who once fled from You, now flee to You.

11.1.5.en: For Adam fled from the face of God and hid among the trees of Paradise, so it was said of him in the Book of Job: “Like a servant who flees from the face of his master, and finds a shadow” (Job 7:2) LXX.

11.1.6.en: Woe to me, if I remain under the shadow, lest it be said afterward: [All those things pass away like a shadow] (Wis 5:9).

11.1.7.en: That you may fight the rulers of this world, of this darkness, the rulers of the wicked (the devil and his hosts).

11.1.8.en: Great is your striving, for you do not see your enemies and yet you overcome them![2]

11.1.9.en: St. Augustine v “And of thy mercy cut off mine enemies”: not because I am worthy of it, but for Your mercy's sake You free me from those who fight against me.

11.1.10.en: Deliver me from those who devise plots; grant me that You free me from distress.

11.1.11.en: “And destroy all them that afflict my soul: for I am thy servant.” Notice again how the request is fulfilled. It is not easily that we receive our requests, but we must make ourselves worthy of it, and contribute from our side what we must contribute, and so we present our requests.

11.1.12.en: (Bare) prayer is naturally not sufficient in itself. The Jews prayed, and the answer was: “When ye make many prayers, I will not hear” (Isa 1:15). Why do you wonder at this if (Ezekiel) himself was not heard? For it was said: [If Noah, Job and Daniel come, they shall not deliver their sons and daughters] (see Ezek 14:14).

11.2.0.en: That you may realize this, we do not only pray, but with prayer we make ourselves worthy to receive the blessings of the present and the future[3].

11.2.1.en: St. John Chrysostom v He who does not take refuge in the sons of men takes refuge in God, and everyone who takes refuge in God, He delivers from his enemies, visible and invisible.

11.3.0.en: Speak unto Rehoboam the son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all Israel in Judah and Benjamin, saying, [3]

11.4.0.en: Thus saith the LORD, Ye shall not go up, nor fight against your brethren:

11.4.1.en: Return every man to his house: for this thing is done of me.

11.4.2.en: And they obeyed the words of the LORD, and returned from going against Jeroboam. [4]

11.4.3.en: When Rehoboam tried to bring the ten tribes back to his obedience, the word of the Lord came to him through Shemaiah the man of God: “Ye shall not go up, nor fight against your brethren: return every man to his house: for this thing is done of me” (2 Chr 11:4). They rejected David, so the Lord counted them as rejecting Him personally!

11.4.4.en: They deprived themselves of being counted the people of God, and not one good king arose from them.

11.4.5.en: Rehoboam set it in his heart to restore the unity of the people by force. But the Lord prevented him from entering into battle with the rest of the tribes, and indeed he stopped.

11.4.6.en: Why did God not permit Rehoboam to go to war against Jeroboam? 1. To punish Solomon for idolatry. 2. God permitted what happened to discipline Rehoboam, who did not consult the Lord before answering Jeroboam and those with him. 3. Because God separated the sheep from the goats so that Israel would not lead Judah astray. If the people were divided into two kingdoms, ten tribes under the name “the kingdom of Israel,” and two tribes under the name “the kingdom of Judah,” the Book of Chronicles, which is concerned with the Temple and worship, almost reckons that the kingdom of Israel, the northern kingdom that broke away from the house of David, does not exist. The king of Judah is considered the recognized one, being king of Judah and Benjamin and all of Israel who returned to Judah and Benjamin. At the same time the people of the schismatic kingdom are counted as brethren of the people of Judah and Benjamin, whom it is not lawful for them to fight, for they are still children of God, who seeks their salvation, not their destruction[4]. 3. That God might assure them that strength is not in the union of Judah with Israel, but in taking refuge in the Lord. 4. The Lord says, “Ye shall not fight against your brethren,” for it is not fitting for brethren under any circumstances to enter into battles together. When Abraham and Lot differed (Gen 12), Abraham reminded his nephew that it was not lawful for them to enter into a battle because they were brethren (Gen 13:8).

11.4.7.en: And when Jacob and Esau differed and entered into something like a battle that lasted all their lives, their descendants continued in bitter enmity for many centuries (Gen 27:41-46; Ps 137:7; Obad 10-13). And when David refused to kill Saul, who was doing all he could to kill David, the Lord rewarded him by handing him the throne and establishing his seat, and from his seed came the Messiah, the Savior of the world, and an intimate friendship formed between the two tribes of Judah and Benjamin after the death of David and Saul, and the two became one kingdom over against the other ten tribes.

11.4.8.en: It is fitting for the believer, in his longing for the salvation of all, not to do this out of blind fanaticism, but in love, through the sense of brotherhood and his awareness of the love of the holy God who gave His only-begotten Son for every person, and also his love for his fellow man. For the believer longs to be joined to all the children of men, those he knows and those he does not know, joined to his contemporaries and those who have departed and those who come after him. He is joined to them in the oneness of true love, in a spiritual kinship that rises above every bodily or blood tie. He is joined with them in the Head, “Jesus Christ,” and all are partners together in everything for ever, especially in holiness in the holy God.

11.4.9.en: v May we who have been made worthy of such mysteries show a life that is fitting for the gift, that is, show conduct of the utmost excellence!...

11.4.10.en: For whether a man is a father or a son or a brother or in any other kinship, he is not counted a true kinsman as when the kinship springs from heavenly relationships. What use is it to be bound by earthly family ties without being bound by spiritual ties?! What benefit is it if we are kinsmen on earth and strangers in heaven?! For the catechumen is a stranger to the believer, since he does not have the same Head spiritually, nor the same Father, nor the same city, nor the same food or garment or table or house, but is different from him.

11.4.11.en: These things belong to the catechumen on earth (that is, he is occupied with ordinary earthly matters), but the other seeks them (as heavenly things) in heaven.

11.4.12.en: One has Christ as King; the other's food is meats that perish and come to an end!

11.4.13.en: One has garments that the moth destroys; the other has the Lord of the angels!

11.4.14.en: One's city is heaven; the other's is earth!

11.4.15.en: So we have nothing in common; in what, then, is our fellowship?!

11.4.16.en: Are we twins, born from one womb?! For this is unable to establish a most perfect kinship.

11.5.0.en: Therefore let us strive to be citizens of the heavenly city![5]

11.5.1.en: St. John Chrysostom “And returned from going against Jeroboam”: Rehoboam responded to the words of the Lord by Shemaiah the man of God, perhaps because he feared failure, since he was not a trained military leader like David his grandfather, but was like his father Solomon, who had no strong military experience. And perhaps after he had built the strongholds and made sure of his military power, he entered into several battles after that against Jeroboam.

11.5.2.en: Moreover, on the other hand, he remained faithful in his worship of the Lord for three years, after which he turned aside to idolatrous worship.

11.6.s.en: 2. Rehoboam's efforts to preserve the two tribes

11.6.0.en: 5 And Rehoboam dwelt in Jerusalem, and built cities for defence in Judah. 6 He built even Bethlehem, and Etam, and Tekoa, 7 And Bethzur, and Shoco, and Adullam, 8 And Gath, and Mareshah, and Ziph, 9 And Adoraim, and Lachish, and Azekah, 10 And Zorah, and Aijalon, and Hebron, which are in Judah and in Benjamin fenced cities. 11 And he fortified the strong holds, and put captains in them, and store of victual, and of oil and wine. 12 And in every several city he put shields and spears, and made them exceeding strong, having Judah and Benjamin on his side.

11.6.1.en: And Rehoboam dwelt in Jerusalem, and built cities for defence in Judah. [5]

11.6.2.en: Without doubt the division of the kingdom shook the image of Israel before the nations and peoples, yet Rehoboam did not care about the nations' mockery of them, but was concerned to fortify the borders of his state and many of the main cities in his kingdom. For in the age of his father Solomon, in the days of peace, there was no need to fortify them. Most of Solomon's work was building and development and production with trade.

11.7.0.en: He built even Bethlehem, and Etam, and Tekoa. [6]

11.7.1.en: He fortified Bethlehem, which is about ten kilometers from Jerusalem, famous as the birthplace of David and of the Son of David, Jesus Christ.

11.7.2.en: Modern excavations confirm the existence of fortifications for the cities mentioned here at that time[6].

11.7.3.en: Rehoboam was concerned to build fortresses in the east and west, and also toward the south, leaving the northern region like an open door, for two main reasons: 1. Rehoboam knew that Jeroboam was on good terms with Egypt, so he feared that Egypt would attack him from the south as a kind of alliance with Jeroboam, who had previously taken refuge in it when Solomon sought to kill him. 2. He left the north like an open door, for on the one hand the priests and Levites who were in the northern kingdom returned to him, where they had found resistance and the putting of priests of the idols and high places in their place. Some of the pious among the people also returned, who refused the worship of idols and wanted to worship the living God. Rehoboam hoped that the people would long to enjoy worship in Jerusalem, especially at the feasts and festivals.

11.8.0.en: And Bethzur, and Shoco, and Adullam. [7]

11.9.0.en: And Gath, and Mareshah, and Ziph. [8]

11.9.1.en: Gath: a city taken by the Jews from the Philistines in the days of Samuel and King David (1 Sam 7:14; 1 Chr 18:1).

11.10.0.en: And Adoraim, and Lachish, and Azekah. [9]

11.11.0.en: And Zorah, and Aijalon, and Hebron, which are in Judah and in Benjamin fenced cities. [10]

11.11.1.en: Hebron: it is Al-Khalil today and is mentioned often; Abraham, Isaac and Jacob dwelt in it, and Sarah, Abraham, Isaac, Rebekah, Leah and Jacob were buried in it. It was one of the cities of the priests and the cities of refuge, and David reigned in it seven years.

11.12.0.en: And he fortified the strong holds, and put captains in them, and store of victual, and of oil and wine. [11]

11.13.0.en: And in every several city he put shields and spears, and made them exceeding strong, having Judah and Benjamin on his side. [12]

11.13.1.en: Rehoboam built cities for defence in the south to face any attack from Egypt [5-12].

11.13.2.en: The fortified cities mentioned are toward the south and west, because he feared Egypt, but we saw the invader coming from Egypt, and the fortified cities did not stop him, for except the Lord keep the city, the watchman waketh but in vain.

11.14.s.en: 3. The return of the priests and Levites

11.14.0.en: 13 And the priests and the Levites that were in all Israel resorted to him out of all their coasts. 14 For the Levites left their suburbs and their possession, and came to Judah and Jerusalem: for Jeroboam and his sons had cast them off from executing the priest's office unto the LORD: 15 And he ordained him priests for the high places, and for the devils, and for the calves which he had made. 16 And after them out of all the tribes of Israel such as set their hearts to seek the LORD God of Israel came to Jerusalem, to sacrifice unto the LORD God of their fathers. 17 So they strengthened the kingdom of Judah, and made Rehoboam the son of Solomon strong, three years: for three years they walked in the way of David and Solomon.

11.14.1.en: It is clear that these ten tribes resisted God by appointing priests for the high places and for the devils and the calves (2 Chr 11:15), and the priests of God and the Levites were compelled to leave the tribes and go to Judah and Jerusalem (2 Chr 11:14).

11.14.2.en: And the priests and the Levites that were in all Israel resorted to him out of all their coasts [13]

11.15.0.en: For the Levites left their suburbs and their possession, and came to Judah and Jerusalem: for Jeroboam and his sons had cast them off from executing the priest's office unto the LORD [14]

11.16.0.en: And he ordained him priests for the high places, and for the devils, and for the calves which he had made. [15]

11.16.1.en: The Book of Kings mentioned the worship of the calves, and here is a reference to another kind of idolatrous worship, whose adherents believed that demons or jinn took the form of goats and lived in desolate places. The origin of the Hebrew word for goats is the jinn. Primitive peoples used to worship what they feared. Sadly, we see here the people of God imitating these peoples and worshiping what they fear.

11.17.0.en: When Jeroboam cast off the worship of the living God, and ordained for himself priests for the high places and the devils and the calves which he had made, he feared that the people would long to return to Jerusalem to worship in the Temple, so he permitted the priests and Levites to go to Jerusalem. They left their suburbs and their possessions, and Rehoboam was strengthened by their presence with the pious of Israel who were faithful in worship [17].

11.17.1.en: It is no wonder that he who rejected God also rejects His servants and longs to be rid of them.

11.17.2.en: At the same time it was to the benefit of these priests and Levites to leave Israel and go to the kingdom of Judah, where the Temple of the Lord and His altar are, and to be rid of the quarrels and vexations that the priests of the high places might stir up against them.

11.17.3.en: And we must not deny that Rehoboam and his people welcomed them, and did not feel that they were a burden on their kingdom after they had lost their suburbs and possessions and fields.

11.17.4.en: They fulfilled what the prophet Isaiah said afterward: “Open ye the gates, that the righteous nation which keepeth the truth may enter in” (Isa 26:2).

11.18.0.en: And after them out of all the tribes of Israel such as set their hearts to seek the LORD God of Israel came to Jerusalem, to sacrifice unto the LORD God of their fathers. [16]

11.18.1.en: There were people in these tribes faithful to the Lord. When the priests and Levites went to Jerusalem, all the righteous and pious Israelites followed them, “such as set their hearts to seek the LORD God of Israel.” They left the inheritance of their fathers and went to dwell in Judah, that they might have full freedom to go to the altar of the Lord, and that they and their children might keep far from any enticement to the worship of goats.

11.18.2.en: These pious ones present a beautiful example for us: 1. They gave priority to the worship of God and care for the salvation of their souls and the souls of their children before any material benefit or temporal comfort and happiness. 2. They clung to the faithful priests of the Lord. It is written in Joshua: “When ye see the ark of the covenant of the LORD your God, and the priests the Levites bearing it, then ye shall remove from your place, and go after it” (Josh 3:3).

11.19.0.en: So they strengthened the kingdom of Judah, and made Rehoboam the son of Solomon strong, three years: for three years they walked in the way of David and Solomon. [17]

11.19.1.en: The kingdom of Judah was strengthened, not only by the increase in numbers, nor by what they brought with them of their personal possessions, but the blessing of the Lord came upon the kingdom through their piety and their prayers and their clinging to the Lord.

11.20.s.en: 4. The wives and children of Rehoboam

11.20.0.en: 18 And Rehoboam took him Mahalath the daughter of Jerimoth the son of David to wife, and Abihail the daughter of Eliab the son of Jesse; 19 Which bare him children; Jeush, and Shamariah, and Zaham. 20 And after her he took Maachah the daughter of Absalom; which bare him Abijah, and Attai, and Ziza, and Shelomith. 21 And Rehoboam loved Maachah the daughter of Absalom above all his wives and his concubines: (for he took eighteen wives, and threescore concubines; and begat twenty and eight sons, and threescore daughters.) 22 And Rehoboam made Abijah the son of Maachah the chief, to be ruler among his brethren: for he thought to make him king. 23 And he dealt wisely, and dispersed of all his children throughout all the countries of Judah and Benjamin, unto every fenced city: and he gave them victual in abundance. And he desired many wives.

11.20.1.en: And Rehoboam took him to wife

11.20.2.en: Mahalath the daughter of Jerimoth the son of David, and Abihail the daughter of Eliab the son of Jesse. [18]

11.20.3.en: Rehoboam was weak in indulging his pleasures, so he sought many wives as his father did. Yet he was wiser than his father, for it seems he did not take wives from the idolatrous women. One of them was of the descendants of Eliab the brother of David [18], another of the descendants of Absalom the son of David [20], and a third of Jerimoth the son of David [18].

11.20.4.en: The name of Jerimoth the son of David has not been mentioned before, and perhaps he was the son of one of David's concubines.

11.21.0.en: Which bare him children; Jeush, and Shamariah, and Zaham [19]

11.22.0.en: And after her he took Maachah the daughter of Absalom; which bare him Abijah, and Attai, and Ziza, and Shelomith. [20]

11.23.0.en: And Rehoboam loved Maachah the daughter of Absalom above all his wives and his concubines: (for he took eighteen wives, and threescore concubines; and begat twenty and eight sons, and threescore daughters.) [21]

11.23.1.en: Rehoboam imitated his father in having many wives and concubines. And yet the book did not indicate that he imitated his father.

11.23.2.en: Of the sons of Solomon, only one person is mentioned, namely Rehoboam, and the rest were not worthy even to have their number mentioned. But as for the sons of Rehoboam, it mentioned their number: twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters.

11.24.0.en: And Rehoboam made Abijah the son of Maachah the chief, to be ruler among his brethren: for he thought to make him king. [22]

11.25.0.en: And he dealt wisely, and dispersed of all his children throughout all the countries of Judah and Benjamin, unto every fenced city: and he gave them victual in abundance.

11.25.2.en: Some see that Rehoboam acted wisely when he distributed the lands of Judah and Benjamin among all his sons, in order to avoid conspiracy against him as Adonijah and Absalom did, so that a schism would occur in the kingdom, so that they would be adversaries to their brother Abijah whom he made chief and ruler among them. On the other hand, as his sons were spread through all the cities, they would preserve the safety of the people and care for the cities he had fortified with walls and their storehouses, and would support their brother if a foreign invasion occurred, and he would also avoid the rise of any revolt in the country against Abijah.

11.25.3.en: Wonderful is Your love, O Holy One!

11.25.4.en: v Wonderful is Your love, and wonderful are Your dispensations, O my Savior!

11.25.5.en: For the salvation of the whole world You chose righteous Abraham!

11.25.6.en: You promised him that he would be a father of many nations!

11.25.7.en: And You chose Isaac his son and Jacob his grandson.

11.25.8.en: From his seed You raised up for Yourself a people, not out of partiality, but that You might come incarnate from his seed, and give Yourself as a redemption for all humanity.

11.25.9.en: v In its disobedience Israel turned aside, and rebelled against You, O Holy One.

11.25.10.en: From among the twelve, You set apart two tribes, Judah and Benjamin, and from them You established the kingdom of Judah, that perhaps they might walk in love and holiness.

11.25.11.en: You did not permit them to fight against the rebellious ten tribes.

11.25.12.en: For You seek brotherly love with holiness!

11.25.13.en: v Many turned aside, even from the two tribes, but You kept a holy remnant.

11.25.14.en: By Your wonderful dispensation You provided in every generation a holy remnant for Yourself!

11.25.15.en: From this remnant You were incarnate of the holy Mary for our redemption.

11.25.16.en: You seek that all humanity be sanctified and that love prevail in it.

11.25.17.en: Wonderful is Your love, O wonderful Holy One!

11.25.18.en: v Grant Your Church to be united with You always.

11.25.19.en: She walks in You, and is filled with love and holiness.

11.25.20.en: She becomes an icon of You, and is made worthy of the heavenly wedding.

11.25.21.en: The holy Father rejoices in her, and the heavenly orders marvel at her!

11.25.22.en: Give me a pure heart filled with love and holiness!
